newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude firms, sweet grades ease in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude firms, sweet grades ease in Gulf.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices firmed slightly Wednesday morning, while domestic grades fell back from recent run-ups after North Sea Brent values eased.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around five cents higher at $20.15-25 a barrel, ranging around even to the second month September WTI cash.

Grade prices saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sell at a 17 cents premium to the marker, down about five cents from Tuesday. Traders said despite declines, the prompt LLS market continued to find support from a lack of Brent coming to the U.S. Gulf.

Other deals were seen for West Texas Sour/Midland at $1.04 and $1.10 under August WTI/Cushing, around steady from Tuesday. WTI/Cushing Postings Plus talked at $1.96-2.00, jumping around the $2.00 mark on the fluctuating Aug/Sep spread.
August Exchange for Physicals were stuck at a two cents premium to the NYMEX screen, trader said.
News in the market was limited to a report Ashland took down a crude unit at its Minnesota refinery after a severe electrical storm caused a fire late Tuesday.
